source.title: Skin-Deep: A Geometric Diagnostic for Alignment Fragility in Large Language Model Representations
source.authors: D. Lee; Jungseob Lee; Seungyoon Lee; Seongtae Hong; Suhyune Son; Sugyeong Eo; Jaehyung Seo; Heuiseok Lim

page_placements.theme: Direction estimation: sensitivity to prompt sets, baselines, labels, layer, normalisation and outlier channels, and estimator reliability

record.tranche_reason: The study ablates several candidate directions and finds model-specific, incomplete refusal effects, refining the single-direction account rather than reproducing its all-layer, all-position intervention.
record.gate_note: The study measures refusal after ablation at one model-specific peak-separation layer. It does not add a direction or test general capability after ablation. The held-out separation, probe, overlap, CKA, GFS, and benign-LoRA results are not recorded as rows because they do not directly measure the direction-ablation refusal effects at issue here. The LoRA results measure outcomes after a separate training intervention, not whether a refusal direction exists or mediates refusal.
record.test_reason: The study projects the Arditi harmful-minus-benign mean-difference direction out of the residual stream and measures harmful-request refusal in six instruct models, with random-direction controls (Table 4, Table 9). That bears directly on V1. Two things set it apart from the original method. Ablation is applied only at one model-specific cPCA peak-separation layer, not at every layer and position. Direction addition and capability preservation are not tested. The results are mixed: marked but incomplete drops in three models, no drop in two, and a floor effect in one. That qualifies V1 rather than reproducing it.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that harmful and benign prompts show a recurring low-rank separation across 21 models, and that selected direction ablations weaken refusal, with the effective direction varying by model. They also argue that their pre-fine-tuning Geometric Fragility Score separates the initially safe model (Gemma) that stays least compliant after benign LoRA. They frame results as tied to tested models and protocols, not a universal refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: The study removes PCA, cPCA, Arditi, or random directions during generation, but only at a model-specific peak-separation layer rather than projecting the difference-in-means direction out of every layer and position. It tests refusal decreases but not direction addition or general capability preservation.
record.method_sensitivity: The direction with a refusal effect varies by model. The selected intervention is applied at a model-specific peak-separation layer. The ablation evaluation uses 100 AdvBench prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: The direction whose single-layer ablation reduces refusal varies by model. PCA-PC1 gives the clearest drop in Llama (0.14→0.02), where the Arditi direction does nothing. All three non-random directions work in Mistral-v0.2. cPCA-PC1 has no effect in Qwen or Gemma. A non-leading PC4 raises Llama refusal to 0.32.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which residual direction mediates refusal at a given layer is model-specific and need not be the difference-in-means direction.

record.problems: Ablations cover six models and one selected layer per model, not every layer and position. Several models have little baseline refusal, and refusal reductions are not universal across directions or models. Other-ability preservation and direction addition are not evaluated. The study notes that refusal and harmful-compliance rates come from different protocols and are not complements.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant ablation rows were left out. Other geometric measurements and benign-LoRA trajectories were omitted because they do not test refusal after the direction ablations or whether that direction mediates refusal.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; ablation at all layers and positions; preservation of other abilities; refusal judge not stated.
No test of affine, cone, or multi-direction structure. Only single directions are ablated one at a time.
Harm judgment is not separated from the refusal decision.
CKA similarity across families is not direction transfer.
Training labels relate to GFS ranking only, not to whether a removable direction exists.

missing.what: Layer index used for each model's ablation, and whether the Arditi direction was computed at that layer or chosen by Arditi's selection procedure
Refusal judge and prompt format (raw vs chat template) for the ablation evaluation; low baselines for Llama and Mistral-v0.3 suggest a non-chat format

record.verdict_notes: All V1-relevant rows come from Table 9 and Appendix C. The study's main contribution is the GFS diagnostic and its LoRA association, which do not test any version. The record's V4 'supports' label for Mistral-v0.2 is removed. Three directions each reducing refusal does not show multi-dimensional refusal, since they may be correlated, and no joint ablation was run. The V1 'challenges' label is softened to limits_scope because the intervention departs from Arditi's all-layer ablation.

versions.untested_parts: Tests removal of the Arditi harmful-minus-benign mean-difference direction at one selected layer. Does not test adding the direction, removal at every layer and position, or preservation of other abilities.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Compares several candidate directions and their refusal effects, but does not test whether refusal geometry is specifically affine, a cone, or another named multi-direction structure.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
Cross-family activation similarity is measured, but transfer of the refusal direction across languages, base/instruct stages, or model variants is not tested.
Checkpoint training labels and benign LoRA outcomes are reported, but the study does not test how refusal-training choices determine whether a removable direction exists.
Hybrid-reasoning Qwen3 models are excluded from the raw-prompt ranking; reasoning-model direction ablation is not tested.
